plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding tiny yellow flower clusters called cyathia. Native to Mexico, it blooms in response to the long nights of late autumn and winter and is a classic holiday plant in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown worldwide as a holiday plant and in frost-free gardens
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves (bracts), not petals. The Aztecs called the plant Cuetlaxochitl and used its sap to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with nodding, saucer-shaped white flowers that often take on a pink blush with age. It flowers in the cold of winter, often pushing through snow, and is prized in shade gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of the Alps and the Apennines in central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true rose; it belongs to the buttercup family and all parts are toxic. Legend says it sprang from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in spectacular clusters of large flowers in the hot season. In the Southern Hemisphere, flowering begins around late spring and early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to February); May to July in the northern tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including northern Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: It is among the most colorful trees in the world, yet it is critically endangered in its native Madagascar, where its natural habitat has largely been lost.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful tree with feathery foliage that bursts into masses of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they drop. In the Southern Hemisphere, blooming peaks in late spring and lingers into early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted widely in South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: In parts of Australia, a falling jacaranda blossom on the head is said to bring good luck, and university students traditionally believe that if a flower falls on you before exams you will pass.
